text:
Avery: Quick all-hands follow-up  dropping a leadership Q&A thread for anything we didn't cover. I'll answer what I can.

Priya: How do we explain our mission to teams that just want model access? They ask: why not use the cloud model APIs?

Avery: We sell predictable outcomes, not raw models. Key points: consistent latency, cost controls, rollout policies, and deployment parity (hosted/dedicated/private). Suggested line: 'Same API, predictable performance and cost at scale.'

Marco: Customer question from infra: are we competing with cloud infra or model providers? Which technical areas are our differentiators?

Avery: We operate as the serving layer between models and infra. Differentiators: runtime optimizations (KV cache, continuous batching), smart routing and fallbacks, and unified deployment semantics. We're not positioning as a model training org.

Sam: For RFPs, should we lead with SLAs or cost numbers? Customers always ask both.

Lina: Marketing needs a short one-pager for procurement. Bullet points only.

Avery: RFP play: lead with SLA/availability and security (private options), then unit economics and cost controls. I'll collaborate with @Lina and @Priya on the draft.

Tanya: Will we open-source parts of the runtime or keep it closed for moat?

Marco: We'll open-source client adapters and tooling; core runtime kernels and scheduler remain proprietary. We'll publish a clear list of OSS components.

Alex (ML): Will we publish recommended model+quantization bundles per workload? Customers want a 'reference stack.'

Priya: Yes. We'll curate bundles in the catalog (e.g., chat: model-X q4_0 + caching; embeddings: model-Y fp16). Make them first-class entries.

Avery: Positioning summary: we're the predictable-serving layer. Compete on operational guarantees, developer ergonomics, and deployment flexibility. Not on training or model R&D.

Sam: Sales objection: 'Why not self-host?' Quick rebuttal?

Avery: Self-hosting means higher ops burden and slower iteration. Offer reserved capacity and private deployments to meet security without ops cost. Themes: speed to product and lower TCO.

Lina: I'll draft the RFP one-pager and a 2-slide positioning nugget for SDRs. @Avery any must-have bullets?

Avery: Include: 'Unified runtime across hosted, dedicated, private' and 'Cost controls: batching, caching, quantization recommendations.' Add a short customer quote if available.

Tanya: Can we add a small SLO example for the one-pager? e.g., p95 < 150ms for small single-turn gen.

Marco: SLO suggestion:
- p50 < 80ms
- p95 < 150ms
- availability >= 99.9%

Avery: Thanks all. Post more follow-ups here and we'll fold into the public summary doc. :sparkles:
